messages:
Nina (CS): Quick thread from today's Sapphire private/VPC dry-run. Blockers: CIDR collision with customer's datacenter, customer-managed CMK rejects decrypt, and audit-forward to their Splunk HEC returns 401. Customer flagged this as a renewal risk for next week. Need P0 triage and owners.
Owen (NetEng): Which CIDR did they pick? I can model overlap and propose short/long-term options.
Nina (CS): They want 10.5.0.0/16; their on-prem VPN uses the same range and they can't renumber until their vendor window in Q3.
Owen (NetEng): If renumbering is impossible: (A) temporary NAT/proxy in our mgmt VPC (fast, +latency +cost), (B) Transit Gateway with route segregation (longer but cleaner). I'll sketch latency/cost and a cutover window.
Tess (Security): KMS note: their CMK key policy only allows principals from their account and denies root. Our decrypt attempt failed with "AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt". We need their role ARN (so we can assume) and they must add our service role to that role's trust policy. Also the CMK key policy must grant kms:Decrypt to the assumed role.
Nina (CS): They provided role arn:aws:iam::777888999000:role/Sapphire-Redwood-Bridge but trust policy currently allows their CI only.
Owen (NetEng): Tess, can you paste a minimal trust policy snippet we can send to the customer?
Tess (Security): Minimal trust policy (paste to customer, replace REDWOOD_ROLE):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDACTED:role/redwood-service"},
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
    }
  ]
}
```
Tess (Security): Also must add a CMK key-policy statement granting "kms:Decrypt" to the assumed role ARN. I'll add exact snippets to the ticket.
log-bot: Forward attempt 2026-06-18T12:07Z to Splunk HEC returned 401 Unauthorized. Response: {"text":"Invalid token"}. Forwarder role: arn:aws:iam::777888999000:role/Sapphire-LogPush. See /var/log/forwarder/sapphire-2026-06-18.log
Nina (CS): They rotated the HEC token yesterday per their note. Likely a config mismatch. Also confirm the forwarder role has permissions to put to the HEC endpoint and VPC egress endpoint if private.
Owen (NetEng): For the temporary NAT/proxy I can prepare a PoC and runbook — expected cutover 30-60m if customer agrees; latency hit estimate: +6-14ms. TGW will take ~2-3 weeks to coordinate. I'll add cost delta.
infra-bot: Created ticket CS-14022: "Sapphire priv-VPC onboarding blockers (CIDR/KMS/Splunk)" assigned to Owen and Tess. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-14022
colin (CS Lead): Marking P0 due to renewal risk. I'll join triage and loop in renewals/legal. Can we sync tomorrow 09:00 PT to finalize ask list before we send to Sapphire?
Nina (CS): Yes — scheduling now. Action items: Owen to upload network diagrams + proxy vs TGW cost/latency and cutover plan; Tess to paste IAM trust and CMK snippets with verification checklist (assume-role smoke, kms:Decrypt test, Splunk ingest test); Nina to draft customer update after sync with owners + ETA.
Sapphire (customer): We'll update the trust policy and rotate HEC token after your sync. Expect confirmation by 13:00 PT tomorrow.
Nina (CS): Thanks team. If we can close these items before their renewal call next week we should be able to de-escalate legal. :thumbsup:"
